title: Storage: why disk is slow and why files exist

claims.text: Patterson's measurements make the asymmetry concrete. Comparing a disk of 1983 with one of 2003, bandwidth improved from 0.6 to 86 megabytes per second, a factor of about 140, while latency improved only from 48.3 to 5.7 milliseconds, a factor of about 8. He quotes David Clark on why: bandwidth problems can be cured with money, latency problems are harder because the speed of light is fixed and you cannot bribe God.

source.title: David A. Patterson, Latency lags bandwidth, Communications of the ACM 47(10):71-75, October 2004

claims.text: The abstraction that hides the device is the file. Among the features Ritchie and Thompson listed for their system in 1974 were a hierarchical file system incorporating demountable volumes, and compatible file, device and inter-process input and output — the second of which is the design decision that lets a program read from a device, a pipe or a stored file without knowing which it has.

source.title: D. M. Ritchie and K. Thompson, The UNIX Time-Sharing System, Communications of the ACM 17(7):365-375, July 1974, doi 10.1145/361011.361061

beats.broke: the persistent store is physically far away in time terms, and it is addressed in blocks rather than in the bytes and structures a program actually holds
beats.fix: put a uniform abstraction over it — a named sequence of bytes that can be opened, read, written and closed — so that programs address data by name and the system handles blocks, devices and placement
beats.cost: the uniformity hides the access cost, so code that would be reasonable in memory becomes pathological against a device where one access costs millions of instructions
beats.interview: why reading the same total number of bytes can take vastly different amounts of time
